name: Grand Command

stars.name: Command Star
stars.notes: Mature, stable K-dwarf with predictable output and low flare activity, providing excellent conditions for long-term military infrastructure and colonization

planets.name: Mercury's Grief
planets.notes: Sun-scorched innermost world with extreme temperature swings. Automated solar energy collection arrays blanket the dayside.

planets.name: Garrison Prime
planets.notes: Fleet Command headquarters world with breathable atmosphere and temperate climate. Population 480 million. Hosts the Admiralty, war colleges, and the largest military shipyard complex in the sector.

planets.name: Muster
planets.notes: Secondary world with thin but breathable atmosphere. Population 65 million. Primary function is troop staging, ground-forces training, and weapons manufacturing.

planets.name: The Brig
planets.notes: Cold, airless rock housing the sector's maximum-security military prison. Underground facilities hold war criminals and classified detainees.

planets.name: Quartermaster
planets.notes: Massive gas giant whose moons serve as fuel depots, munitions stockpiles, and fleet staging anchorages. The moon Commissary hosts a population of 12,000 logistics personnel.

planets.name: Sentinel
planets.notes: Smaller gas giant with extensive ring system. Rings are seeded with automated defense platforms and sensor arrays.

planets.name: Exile
planets.notes: Frozen outer world used for cold-weather warfare training and long-range communications relay stations.

anomalies.name: The Admiralty Veil
anomalies.notes: A dense shell of artificial and natural electromagnetic interference surrounding Garrison Prime that scrambles long-range scans and prevents unauthorized surveillance of military installations

asteroid_belts.name: The Munitions Belt
asteroid_belts.notes: Rich metallic belt actively mined for warship construction materials. Heavily patrolled; unauthorized prospecting is a capital offense.

stations.name: Admiralty Station
stations.notes: Supreme military command center for the entire sector. The most heavily defended station in Terran space, surrounded by a permanent battle group of 40+ warships.

stations.name: Forge Orbital
stations.notes: Twelve construction slips capable of building dreadnoughts from keel to commission. Current output is approximately four capital ships per standard year.

stations.name: Camp Valor
stations.notes: Largest ground-forces training installation in the sector. Combined arms, urban warfare, and zero-G combat facilities spread across 40,000 square kilometers.

stations.name: Depot Anchor
stations.notes: Central logistics hub managing supply chains across the sector. Automated warehouses contain six months of wartime material reserves.

faction_control.notes: Absolute military jurisdiction. Grand Command is the seat of Terran naval power in the rimward sectors. Civilian presence is limited to authorized contractors and diplomatic missions.

history: Established in 2352 as a forward naval base, Grand Command grew over three centuries into the primary military hub for all Terran operations beyond the core worlds, selected for its stable star and abundance of habitable and resource-rich worlds.

During the First Kethrani War in 2488-2501, Grand Command served as the staging point for the decisive Hammer Offensive that broke the Kethrani siege of the Contested Marches and established Terran dominance in the region.

The system has survived two assassination attempts against sitting Fleet Admirals, a sabotage campaign targeting Forge Orbital in 2639, and a brief mutiny aboard Admiralty Station in 2671 that was suppressed within six hours. Each incident led to further tightening of the system's already formidable security.
description: Grand Command is the beating heart of Terran military power in the rimward sectors. Seven worlds orbit a steady orange-yellow star, and every one of them serves the war machine. Garrison Prime is a world of parade grounds, war colleges, and shipyards, its cities laid out in geometric precision reflecting military planning rather than organic growth. Muster trains the soldiers. The Brig holds the condemned. Quartermaster fuels and arms the fleets. Even the frozen outer world of Exile serves as a training ground and relay station. There is no wasted space in Grand Command; every world, every moon, every asteroid has been requisitioned.

The system's military significance is unparalleled. Admiralty Station coordinates naval operations across dozens of systems, and Forge Orbital produces capital warships at an industrial pace. The permanent battle group surrounding Admiralty Station alone represents enough firepower to devastate a planet. Camp Valor on Muster's surface graduates 200,000 trained soldiers per year. The sector's entire logistical spine runs through Depot Anchor. If Grand Command were to fall, Terran military power in the rimward sectors would collapse within months.

The system's very importance makes it a target, and its commanders know it. Security is layered, redundant, and occasionally paranoid. The Admiralty Veil surrounding Garrison Prime makes the planet essentially invisible to long-range scanning, and the inner system's patrol density is the highest in Terran space. Yet the 2671 mutiny revealed that the greatest threat may come from within. The incident's causes remain classified, but rumors persist of ideological fractures within the officer corps—disagreements about the direction of the war that even Grand Command's rigid discipline cannot entirely suppress.
